title: Runway mix shift trigger and role-swap scenarios - Mar 2025
content:
Purpose:
Short workbook to capture an operational heuristic for when to shift mix (runway-preserving price increases, slab swaps, or role-swap hiring) under sudden token-price pressure or sustained slower revenue. Intended for Finance + GTM + Eng leadership to run quick checks and agree guardrails.

Key summary (one line):
If 12-week runway falls below 16 weeks under medium-probability stress, trigger a three-step playbook: 1) immediate non-headcount cost freezes, 2) temporary tiered price lift on top-20% of customers (2–8%), 3) role-swap hiring (defer senior hires, shift to mid-level contractors for burst).

Assumptions (base case):
- Starting runway: 40 weeks (current cash, no new financing)
- Monthly burn base (Mar 2025): $3.6M (Salaries $2.4M, Cloud/GPU $0.7M, G&A $0.5M)
- Token price shock scenarios modeled as a change in unit cost-to-revenue ratio (UTR): base UTR=0.28, mild shock +0.05, medium shock +0.12, severe shock +0.24
- Take-rate elasticity estimates (rough): small customers elasticity = -1.2, mid = -0.6, enterprise = -0.15
- Headcount by role (current, FTEs): Eng 60, Infra/SRE 18, Product/Design 14, Sales/CS 40, Finance/Legal/People 18, Total FTEs=150

Decision triggers (heuristic):
- Green (no action): runway >= 28 weeks
- Yellow (prepare): runway 18–27 weeks -> implement pricing-sensitivity experiments, hire freeze for IC & above, re-evaluate contracts
- Red (act): runway < 18 weeks -> execute Tiered Surge Trigger (see playbook)

Scenario table (runway projection in weeks) - three scenarios modeled for 12-month forward with no hiring changes except described actions. Numbers are rounded.

CSV style table (Scenario label, Monthly burn after adjustments, Cash runway weeks):
Base-case, $3.6M, 40
Mild-token-shock (UTR +0.05), $3.92M, 37
Medium-token-shock (UTR +0.12), $4.27M, 33
Severe-token-shock (UTR +0.24), $4.98M, 28
Demand-collapse (20% revenue drop), $4.32M, 30
Hybrid (medium shock + demand -10%), $4.7M, 26

Headcount phasing matrix (quick view):
- Immediate (0–12w): hiring freeze for senior ICs and above, pause new grad hires, contractor cap +15% for support roles
- Near-term (12–24w): review top 15% of roles by compensation for voluntary reduced hours/temporary role-swap to contractor
- Medium-term (24–52w): apply selective reduced comp increases, re-evaluate Dedicated vs Hosted product investments

Role-swap illustrative calculation (one example):
- Role: Senior Infra Eng (comp fully-loaded $30k/mo). Option A: hire as FTE -> $30k/mo. Option B: role-swap to contractor/perf-hire -> $18k/mo (conservative). Delta = $12k/mo saved per seat.
- To save $200k/mo in burn, need ~17 role-swaps (200/12 ≈ 16.7).

Pricing sensitivity quick-run (to estimate revenue impact of suggested temporary increases):
- Focus on top-20% customers by revenue (account for ≈64% of ARR). Targeted small lift (2–8%) on tiered bands.
- Example bands and expected churn impact (elasticity assumptions):
Band A (top 5%): expected elasticity -0.15 -> 5% price lift -> revenue +4.25% net, negligible churn in 12w window
Band B (next 15%): elasticity -0.6 -> 4% price lift -> revenue +2.4% net, churn risk ~3% over 6 months
Band C (remaining customer book): avoid immediate increases; instead tighten quotas/trials and push usage-best-practices

Simple sensitivity model outputs: (assume ARR from top-20% = $40M annual)
- Option: 5% lift on top 20% -> immediate annualized revenue +$2.0M -> monthly effect ~+$166k; hit to churn in year 1 estimated -$120k -> net +$46k/mo equivalent.
- Option: 8% lift on top 20% -> +$3.2M annualized -> +$266k/mo; churn risk -$250k annual -> net +$47k/mo (front-loaded benefit).

Net effect vs burn: these pricing moves buy ~1–2 weeks of runway per 5–8% lift in top accounts depending on churn timing and collection; therefore treat as tactical, not structural.

Runway consequence matrix (if we apply playbook):
- If medium shock and we 1) freeze hiring, 2) swap 10 senior FTEs to contractors, 3) apply 5% top-20% lift -> estimated burn reduction = $150k hiring + $120k role-swap + pricing net +$46k => combined ~ $316k/mo -> runway increases by ~2.5–3 weeks relative to no-action baseline.

Operational playbook (Tiered Surge Trigger):
Trigger condition: 12-week forward runway < 16 weeks under stress scenario AND CFO approval.
Steps (ordered, with owners):
1) Immediate cost freeze (Finance) - freeze non-essential vendor spend, pause noncritical hiring. Owner: Finance Lead (Maya) - ETA 48h
2) Customer-targeted price experiments (GTM/Product) - rapid A/B on 2% vs 6% on top 3 enterprise accounts; measure retention/usage 2-week cadence. Owner: Head of Revenue (Jonas) - ETA 1 week
3) Role-swap rollout (Eng/People) - identify 8–20 high-comp roles where contractor swap reduces burn. Communication: voluntary first, then temporary offers. Owner: People + Eng leads - ETA 2–4 weeks
4) Dedicated capacity deferral (Product/Infra) - shift lower-priority Dedicated pool expansions to queue; can reduce cloud spend via spot/quantization pilot. Owner: Product Infra - ETA 2 weeks
5) Executive cadence (Weekly) - CFO + CEO + Head of Eng + Head of Revenue review runway, triggers, and outcomes.

Open questions / data needed (next 7 days):
- Break down of ARR by 50/20/30 split by counts and ARR for sensitivity bands (need precise top-20%), last updated Feb 2025 (owner: Revenue ops)
- Role-level total comp and contract replacement market rates for up to 25 candidate roles (owner: People Ops)
- Contract/Cancellation CLA windows for top 40 accounts to model realistic churn timing (owner: Customer Success)

Immediate action items (owners):
- Finance to produce an updated 12-week rolling burn model with spot/gpu variance bands (Avery) - due Mar 19
- Revenue ops to slice ARR into proposed bands and return elasticity sensitivity (Jonas) - due Mar 20
- People Ops to run a contractor market-quote for senior infra and eng leads (Priya) - due Mar 22

Notes and context (working doc):
- This is intentionally conservative on elasticity for enterprise; small short-term price lifts typically have low elastic response if product lock-in high.
- Role-swap is disruptive and should be voluntary where possible; messaging and retention levers (equity, time-limited bonuses) are separate conversation.
- On the product side, short-term cloud savings via quantization/compaction pilots can be meaningful but usually take 8–12 weeks to operationalize; treat as medium-term complement.

Appendix (raw numbers snapshot):
- Cash balance (Mar 1 2025): $36M
- Monthly burn breakout: Salaries $2,400,000 | Cloud/GPU $700,000 | Other OpEx $300,000 | Rent/benefits $200,000 | Sales & Marketing $0 (embedded above) -> total $3,600,000
- Average fully-loaded FTE cost (company-wide): $20k/mo

This sheet is a living artifact: change the base UTR, elasticity numbers, or contractor rates and re-run the "Role-swap illustrative calculation". Use JIRA-FIN-342 to track final executive decisions.
